name: Customer Type and Behaviour Risk
description: Inherent-risk factors relating to who the customer is and how they behave towards the institution. Covers politically exposed persons, non-residents, cash-intensive businesses, complex structures, reluctance to provide information and negative news. Used as the customer-risk dimension of an enterprise-wide or customer risk assessment.

sources.text: FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach (sector-specific guidance series, general principles)
FATF Recommendations, Recommendation 1 and Interpretive Note (assessing risks and applying a risk-based approach)
Wolfsberg Group, Guidance on a Risk Based Approach for Managing Money Laundering Risks (2006)

exposure.rationale: Generic customer-type risk: PEPs, non-residents, cash-intensive and complex-structure customers.

indicators.name: Politically exposed person as customer or controller
indicators.canon: Politically exposed person as customer or controller
indicators.desc: The customer, a beneficial owner or a controller is a domestic or foreign PEP, or a family member or close associate of one.
indicators.ctx: The customer, a beneficial owner or a controller is a domestic or foreign PEP, or a family member or close associate of one.
indicators.fp: Many PEPs, particularly domestic or low-level officials, are lawfully wealthy and low risk once source of wealth is understood.

indicators.name: Non-resident customer without clear rationale
indicators.desc: Customer resides outside the institution's market and cannot explain why they need an account or service here.
indicators.ctx: Customer resides outside the institution's market and cannot explain why they need an account or service here.
indicators.fp: Expatriates, students, property investors and cross-border workers often have legitimate need.

indicators.name: Cash-intensive business
indicators.desc: Customer's business relies heavily on cash receipts, making revenue difficult to verify against stock, costs or card use.
indicators.ctx: Customer's business model relies heavily on cash receipts (e.g. retail, restaurants, car washes, vending), making revenue hard to verify.
indicators.fp: Cash-heavy trades are common and legitimate; indicator only grows with volume out of line with peers.

indicators.name: Complex or unnecessarily layered structure
indicators.canon: Complex layered structure without commercial rationale
indicators.desc: Multiple tiers of entities, trusts or foundations, often across secrecy or low-transparency jurisdictions, with no evident business or tax reason.
indicators.ctx: Customer is part of a multi-layer or multi-jurisdiction structure without an evident commercial purpose.
indicators.fp: Large groups, funds and tax-efficient structures can be complex for lawful reasons.

indicators.name: Unwillingness or inability to provide information
indicators.canon: Refusal or delay in answering due diligence requests
indicators.desc: Customer or counterparty delays, refuses or gives incomplete or evasive responses to KYC, refresh or request-for-information enquiries.
indicators.ctx: Customer delays, refuses or gives evasive answers to KYC or refresh requests, or withdraws when questioned.
indicators.fp: Customers may be privacy-conscious, unfamiliar with requirements or have genuinely lost documents.

indicators.name: Adverse media on customer or associates
indicators.canon: Adverse media on customer or associates
indicators.desc: Credible negative news, enforcement notices or investigations link the customer, its owners or associates to criminal, corrupt or regulated-sector misconduct.
indicators.ctx: Credible negative news links the customer or associated parties to financial crime, corruption or regulatory action.
indicators.fp: Name matches, old or unproven allegations and unrelated namesakes are common.

indicators.name: Customer reluctant to disclose beneficial owner or purpose
indicators.canon: Reluctance to disclose beneficial ownership or control
indicators.desc: Customer or intermediary is vague, delayed or inconsistent when asked who owns, controls or ultimately benefits from an account, entity or funds.
indicators.ctx: Customer is vague about who ultimately benefits from the account or the intended use of funds.
indicators.fp: Trustees, professionals and privacy-sensitive clients may need time to supply details.

indicators.name: Customer with prior regulatory, criminal or sanctions history
indicators.canon: Prior regulatory, criminal or enforcement history
indicators.desc: Customer or principal has previous convictions, enforcement or disciplinary action, or has been exited by another institution.
indicators.ctx: Customer or principal has previous convictions, enforcement action, or has been exited by another institution.
indicators.fp: Spent or unrelated histories may not indicate current risk.

indicators.name: Occupation or business inconsistent with wealth
indicators.canon: Occupation or business inconsistent with wealth
indicators.desc: Declared occupation, age or business does not plausibly explain the scale of assets or funds.
indicators.ctx: Declared occupation, age or business does not plausibly explain the scale of assets or funds.
indicators.fp: Inheritance, windfalls or undeclared secondary income can explain gaps.

indicators.name: Customer in a high-risk sector
indicators.desc: Customer operates in a sector with elevated misuse risk, such as precious metals, gambling, crypto, arms, or money transfer.
indicators.ctx: Customer operates in a sector with elevated misuse risk, such as precious metals, gambling, crypto, arms, or money transfer.
indicators.fp: Most firms in these sectors are regulated and compliant.

indicators.name: Customer frequently changes details
indicators.canon: Frequent changes of customer or entity details
indicators.desc: Customer or entity repeatedly changes name, address, contact details, directors, signatories or ownership.
indicators.ctx: Customer repeatedly changes name, address, contact, signatories or ownership shortly after onboarding.
indicators.fp: Life events, relocations and restructures legitimately change details.
